memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If people are fighting and hit a pregnant woman and she gives birth prematurely but there is no serious injury, the offender must be fined whatever the woman's husband demands and the court allows. But if there is serious injury, you are to take life for life," - Exodus 21:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Even in the chaos of a fight, God's law reaches out to protect a pregnant woman and the child she carries. Harm done to her and her baby is not brushed aside as an accident of the scuffle; it demands accountability. When serious injury results, the full weight of justice applies. God does not treat the vulnerable life within the womb as insignificant.

This reveals the tender attention of God toward those who cannot speak or defend themselves. The unborn child, the mother caught in danger — both matter to Him. Throughout Scripture we see this same heart, from David marvelling that God knit him together in his mother's womb (Ps 139:13-16) to the leap of unborn John at the presence of Jesus (Luke 1:41). Life is precious to God from its very beginning.

In a world that often measures worth by usefulness or strength, this is a steadying truth. Your value never rested on what you could do or produce. You were treasured by God before you drew your first breath. And that same God calls His people to cherish and protect the weakest among us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I see every human life — even the smallest and weakest — as precious to God?
How can I speak up or care for those who cannot defend themselves?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You treasure life from its very first moment. Give me Your heart for the vulnerable and the voiceless, and help me protect what You hold precious. Amen.
